page: Amazon Web Services c6a.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.6 GHz, delivering 48 virtual CPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory resources total 96 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU ratio characteristic of compute-intensive infrastructure. The instance does not include local disk storage, relying on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network throughput of 19 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects strong raw computational throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests (71,762.56) and single-core stress-ng evaluations (2,991.79). Its PassMark CPU overall score of 54,220.54 and encryption test result of 56,849.38 also rank in the top quartile, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions. Geekbench ray tracing scores (55,695.0) and image processing metrics (14,661.0) highlight significant floating-point performance. In contrast, memory bandwidth measurements, such as large-block read operations at 66.3 GB/sec and write operations at 30.23 GB/sec, register in the middle tier, aligning with DDR4 bus constraints under heavy saturation.

In terms of efficiency and operational tradeoffs, c6a.12xlarge leverages high core density to offer strong compute-per-dollar value for heavily parallelized workloads. However, the absence of onboard NVMe storage necessitates external EBS volumes, introducing storage I/O latency dependencies. Furthermore, with only 2 GB of RAM per vCPU, applications requiring large in-memory caches will face memory limitations before CPU saturation occurs.

This instance profile is best suited for compute-bound operations that scale horizontally across threads. Appropriate workloads include continuous integration and build systems, video encoding, batch image rendering, distributed web serving, and high-throughput data compression.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by a 48-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R13 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Designed around the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 24 physical cores running at 3.6 GHz alongside 96 GB of DDR4 system memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration includes no discrete graphics hardware and provides no integrated local storage, requiring attached network volumes, while supplying a baseline network bandwidth of 19 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute performance across stress-ng, PassMark CPU tests, and cryptographic operations, balanced by median-tier uncached DDR4 memory throughput. The system delivers dense multi-threaded processing power without the overhead of unused memory capacity, making it a viable deployment target for distributed batch processing, parallelized software compilation, media transcoding, and compute-heavy microservices.
